10-1.title: Rivers, Dynasties, and the Mandate of Heaven
10-1.learn:
KEY IDEAS — CHINA'S RIVERS, DYNASTIES, AND THE MANDATE OF HEAVEN

Chinese civilization grew along two great rivers: the YELLOW RIVER (Huang He) and the YANGTZE River. Like other early civilizations, China grew where river floods left rich soil for farming. The Yellow River is sometimes called 'China's Sorrow' because its floods could be deadly.

China was ruled by families called DYNASTIES. A dynasty is a series of rulers from the same family, where power passes down from parent to child. When one ruling family was overthrown, a new dynasty took its place; this rise and fall is called the dynastic cycle.

The Chinese explained who had the right to rule with the MANDATE OF HEAVEN. This was the idea that Heaven (a divine power) gave a ruler the right to rule — but ONLY as long as he ruled WISELY and FAIRLY. If a dynasty became cruel, weak, or brought disasters, people believed it had LOST the Mandate of Heaven, and it was acceptable to replace it with a new, better ruler. The Mandate of Heaven both justified a ruler's power and gave a reason to overthrow a bad one. Remember: Mandate of Heaven = China's idea of the right to rule.

questions.question: Along which two rivers did Chinese civilization grow?
questions.explanation: China grew along the Yellow and Yangtze rivers.

questions.question: A series of rulers from the same family is called a what?
questions.explanation: A ruling family line is called a dynasty.

questions.question: What was the Mandate of Heaven?

choices.A: A set of written laws on stone
choices.B: The idea that Heaven gave a ruler the right to rule if he ruled well
choices.C: A trade route to the west

questions.explanation: The Mandate of Heaven gave rulers the right to rule, but only if they ruled wisely.

questions.question: According to the Mandate of Heaven, when could a ruler lose the right to rule?

choices.B: Only when he died of old age
choices.C: When he became cruel, weak, or unfair

questions.explanation: A cruel or weak ruler was believed to lose the Mandate of Heaven.

questions.question: Why did rivers matter for early Chinese farming?

choices.B: They had no effect on farming
choices.C: Floods left rich soil for crops
choices.D: They were used only for swimming

questions.explanation: River floods provided fertile soil for farming.

questions.question: In a dynasty, how does power usually pass on?

choices.D: From parent to child in the same family

questions.explanation: In a dynasty, power passes down within one family.

questions.question: Why is the Yellow River sometimes called 'China's Sorrow'?

choices.C: It was too small to use

questions.explanation: The Yellow River's dangerous floods earned it the name 'China's Sorrow.'

questions.question: How did the Mandate of Heaven justify overthrowing a ruler?

choices.A: It never allowed any change of ruler
choices.B: A bad ruler was believed to have lost Heaven's support
choices.C: It required a vote of the people

questions.explanation: If a ruler lost Heaven's favor, replacing him was seen as acceptable.

questions.question: The repeated rise and fall of dynasties is known as the what?
questions.explanation: The pattern of dynasties rising and falling is the dynastic cycle.

questions.question: Which civilization is correctly matched with the Mandate of Heaven?
questions.explanation: The Mandate of Heaven was a Chinese idea.

questions.question: What is the other name for the Yellow River used in the lesson?
questions.explanation: The Yellow River is also called the Huang He.

questions.question: Which word best completes this sentence: 'A divine power that gave a ruler the right to rule was called the Mandate of ___.'
questions.explanation: The right to rule came from the Mandate of Heaven.

questions.question: A new ruling family takes power after the old one is overthrown. What has just happened?
questions.explanation: When a new family takes power, a new dynasty begins.

questions.question: Both the Yellow and Yangtze rivers were important to China mainly because they

choices.C: provided water and fertile soil for farming

questions.explanation: The rivers gave China water and fertile soil for farming.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT part of the Mandate of Heaven idea?

choices.A: Heaven gives a ruler the right to rule
choices.B: A ruler must rule wisely and fairly
choices.C: A cruel ruler can lose Heaven's support
choices.D: Rulers are chosen by a public vote

questions.explanation: A public vote was not part of the Mandate of Heaven; rulers were not elected by the people.

questions.question: A dynasty becomes cruel, loses wars, and disasters strike. According to Chinese belief, what does this MEAN?

choices.A: The dynasty has gained more power
choices.B: The dynasty has lost the Mandate of Heaven
choices.D: A new philosophy has been born

questions.explanation: Disasters and cruelty were signs a dynasty had lost the Mandate of Heaven.

questions.question: The Mandate of Heaven was useful to rulers because it

choices.C: explained who had the right to rule

questions.explanation: The Mandate of Heaven explained who had the right to rule.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly describes a dynasty?

choices.A: A group of farmers who share land
choices.B: A series of rulers from the same family

questions.explanation: A dynasty is a series of rulers from the same family.

questions.question: Like Egypt's Nile and Mesopotamia's Tigris, China's rivers were important because all of these civilizations

choices.A: grew near rivers that helped farming

questions.explanation: Each civilization grew near a river that helped farming.

questions.question: Put these in the correct order for the dynastic cycle.

choices.A: A new dynasty rises, rules well, then weakens and falls, and another rises
choices.B: A dynasty rules forever and never changes
choices.C: People vote, then a king is crowned for life
choices.D: Rivers flood, then all rulers disappear

questions.explanation: In the dynastic cycle a new dynasty rises, rules, weakens, falls, and another rises in its place.

questions.question: Which body of water is matched correctly with China?
questions.explanation: The Yangtze River is one of China's two great rivers.

questions.question: Who did the Chinese believe gave a ruler the right to rule?
questions.explanation: A divine power called Heaven was believed to grant the right to rule.

questions.question: Why might the Mandate of Heaven cause people to support overthrowing a cruel ruler?

choices.A: Because a cruel ruler had likely lost Heaven's support
choices.C: Because cruel rulers always live longest
choices.D: Because they wanted no ruler at all

questions.explanation: A cruel ruler was believed to have lost Heaven's support, so replacing him seemed acceptable.

questions.question: Which is the BEST short definition of the Mandate of Heaven?

choices.A: China's idea of the right to rule
choices.B: A river that floods every year
choices.C: A wall built to stop invaders

questions.explanation: The Mandate of Heaven was China's idea of the right to rule.

questions.question: In a dynasty, who would most likely become the next ruler?
questions.explanation: In a dynasty, power passes from parent to child, so the ruler's child would usually rule next.

questions.question: Which of these was a danger of living near the Yellow River?
questions.explanation: The Yellow River's deadly floods were a real danger, earning it the name 'China's Sorrow.'

questions.question: The Mandate of Heaven did TWO things at once. What were they?

choices.C: It justified a ruler's power AND gave a reason to overthrow a bad ruler
choices.D: It ended trade and started war

questions.explanation: The Mandate of Heaven both justified a ruler's power and gave a reason to overthrow a bad one.

questions.question: A teacher says, 'Power passed down from parent to child in one family.' Which term fits?
questions.explanation: Power passing from parent to child in one family describes a dynasty.

questions.question: Which statement about China's early civilization is TRUE?

choices.A: It grew far from any water
choices.B: It grew along the Yellow and Yangtze rivers
choices.C: It had no rulers at all
choices.D: It was ruled by the Mongols first

questions.explanation: China's early civilization grew along the Yellow and Yangtze rivers.

questions.question: Which question would a Chinese person use the Mandate of Heaven to answer?

choices.C: 'Who has the right to rule, and when may a ruler be replaced?'

questions.explanation: The Mandate of Heaven answered who had the right to rule and when a ruler could be replaced.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of China's two great rivers from the lesson?
questions.explanation: The Tigris River is in Mesopotamia, not one of China's two great rivers (the Yellow/Huang He and the Yangtze).

questions.question: A good ruler keeps the Mandate of Heaven as long as he
questions.explanation: A ruler kept the Mandate of Heaven only as long as he ruled wisely and fairly.

questions.question: Why did floods help farmers even though they could be dangerous?

choices.A: They washed away all the crops
choices.B: They left behind rich soil for growing crops

questions.explanation: Floods left behind rich soil that was good for growing crops.

questions.question: Which pair correctly matches an idea with the civilization that used it?
questions.explanation: The Mandate of Heaven belonged to China.

questions.question: Imagine a weak dynasty that lets bandits raid villages and ignores starving farmers. Many Chinese would say this dynasty

choices.B: has earned more of Heaven's favor
choices.C: is losing the Mandate of Heaven and may be replaced

questions.explanation: A weak, neglectful dynasty was seen as losing the Mandate of Heaven and could rightly be replaced.

questions.question: What is the main reason early people settled near rivers like the Yellow and Yangtze?

choices.A: Rivers gave water and fertile land for farming
choices.D: Rivers had the Mandate of Heaven

questions.explanation: Rivers provided water and fertile land that made farming possible.

questions.question: Which of these best shows the dynastic cycle in action?

choices.A: One family rules China without change for all of history
choices.B: A strong family rises, later weakens, falls, and a new family takes power
choices.C: The people elect a new leader every year
choices.D: A river decides who will be king

questions.explanation: The dynastic cycle is a strong family rising, weakening, falling, and a new family taking power.

questions.question: The word 'mandate' in 'Mandate of Heaven' is closest in meaning to

choices.B: a command or right given to someone

questions.explanation: A mandate is a command or right given to someone, here the right to rule given by Heaven.

questions.question: Which of these did the Mandate of Heaven NOT depend on?

choices.C: How much silk a ruler owned

questions.explanation: Keeping the Mandate of Heaven depended on ruling wisely and fairly to keep Heaven's favor, not on how much silk a ruler owned.

questions.question: Why is the Yellow River nicknamed 'China's Sorrow' rather than 'China's Joy'?

choices.A: Because its floods could destroy homes and take lives
choices.C: Because it carried too much gold
choices.D: Because it was the smallest river

questions.explanation: The nickname 'China's Sorrow' came from the river's deadly, destructive floods.

10-2.title: Confucius, Laozi, and Chinese Thinkers
10-2.learn:
KEY IDEAS — CHINA'S GREAT THINKERS

Ancient China produced famous teachers whose ideas guided life for centuries. These belief systems are called philosophies — ways of thinking about how people should live and how rulers should govern.

CONFUCIUS taught CONFUCIANISM. He stressed RESPECT, especially respect for elders and family, along with good manners, education, and order. Confucius believed leaders should set a GOOD EXAMPLE so the people would follow. His teachings shaped Chinese family life and government for thousands of years.

LAOZI is connected with DAOISM (also spelled Taoism). Daoism taught living SIMPLY and in HARMONY with nature, rather than seeking power or following lots of rules.

HAN FEI ZI taught LEGALISM. Legalism is very different: it taught that people need STRICT LAWS and HARSH PUNISHMENTS to keep order, because rulers should be feared, not just admired. So China had three big ideas: Confucianism (respect and good example), Daoism (harmony with nature), and Legalism (strict laws). Remember which teacher goes with which idea.

questions.question: Which teacher founded Confucianism?
questions.explanation: Confucius founded Confucianism.

questions.question: What did Confucius mainly teach?

choices.A: Respect, good manners, and leaders setting a good example

questions.explanation: Confucius taught respect, manners, and good leadership by example.

questions.question: Daoism (Taoism), connected with Laozi, taught people to do what?

choices.A: Live simply and in harmony with nature
choices.C: Seek as much power as possible

questions.explanation: Daoism taught simple living in harmony with nature.

questions.question: Which philosophy taught that strict laws and harsh punishments keep order?
questions.explanation: Legalism relied on strict laws and harsh punishments.

questions.question: Who is connected with the philosophy of Daoism?
questions.explanation: Laozi is associated with Daoism.

questions.question: Who taught Legalism?
questions.explanation: Han Fei Zi taught Legalism.

questions.question: According to Confucius, how should a good leader behave?

choices.B: Set a good example for the people to follow

questions.explanation: Confucius said leaders should lead by good example.

questions.question: These belief systems about how to live and govern are called what?
questions.explanation: Ways of thinking about life and government are philosophies.

questions.question: How is Legalism MOST different from Confucianism?

choices.A: Legalism relies on fear and harsh laws, not respect and good example

questions.explanation: Legalism uses strict, harsh rule, while Confucianism uses respect and example.

questions.question: Confucius's teachings shaped Chinese what for thousands of years?
questions.explanation: Confucianism shaped Chinese family life and government for ages.

questions.question: What is a philosophy?

choices.B: A way of thinking about how people should live and how rulers should govern

questions.explanation: A philosophy is a way of thinking about how people should live and how rulers should govern.

questions.question: Which philosophy is connected with Laozi?
questions.explanation: Laozi is connected with Daoism.

questions.question: A leader rules only by scaring people with harsh punishments. Which philosophy does this match?
questions.explanation: Ruling by fear and harsh punishment matches Legalism.

questions.question: Confucius placed great importance on respect for whom?
questions.explanation: Confucius stressed respect, especially for elders and family.

questions.question: Which philosophy taught living in harmony with nature?
questions.explanation: Daoism taught living simply and in harmony with nature.

questions.question: Which of these did Confucius value? Choose the BEST answer.
questions.explanation: Confucius valued education, good manners, respect, and order.

questions.question: Which teacher is correctly paired with his idea?
questions.explanation: Laozi is paired with Daoism.

questions.question: A Daoist would most likely advise a person to

choices.A: make as many strict laws as possible
choices.C: live simply and follow the natural way

questions.explanation: Daoism advised living simply and in harmony with nature, the natural way.

questions.question: Which philosophy is NOT one of China's three big ideas from the lesson?
questions.explanation: China's three big ideas were Confucianism, Daoism, and Legalism; Democracy was a Greek idea.

questions.question: Han Fei Zi believed a ruler should be

choices.B: feared, with strict laws and harsh punishments

questions.explanation: Han Fei Zi's Legalism taught that rulers should be feared, using strict laws and harsh punishments.

questions.question: Confucius believed that if a leader set a good example, the people would
questions.explanation: Confucius taught that a leader who set a good example would be followed by the people.

questions.question: Which philosophy most strongly focused on order in the family and society through respect?
questions.explanation: Confucianism focused on order through respect for elders, family, and good behavior.

questions.question: Daoism is also spelled which other way?
questions.explanation: Daoism is also spelled Taoism.

questions.question: Which is the BEST example of a Confucian value in everyday life?

choices.A: A child showing respect to a grandparent
choices.B: A king jailing people for tiny mistakes
choices.C: A person ignoring all rules to wander in nature

questions.explanation: A child respecting a grandparent reflects the Confucian value of respect for elders and family.

questions.question: Which is the BEST example of Legalism in action?

choices.A: Teaching children to honor their parents
choices.B: Living quietly and in tune with nature
choices.C: Punishing even small crimes harshly to keep order

questions.explanation: Punishing even small crimes harshly to keep order is an example of Legalism.

questions.question: Which teacher's ideas shaped Chinese family life and government for thousands of years?
questions.explanation: Confucius's teachings shaped Chinese family life and government for thousands of years.

questions.question: How does Daoism MOST differ from Legalism?

choices.A: Daoism seeks harmony with nature, while Legalism relies on strict laws and punishment
choices.C: Daoism uses harsh punishments and Legalism loves nature

questions.explanation: Daoism seeks harmony with nature, while Legalism relies on strict laws and harsh punishment.

questions.question: Which word group best describes Confucianism?
questions.explanation: Confucianism is best described by respect, manners, order, and leading by good example.

questions.question: A ruler asks three advisers how to govern. Which adviser is the LEGALIST?

choices.A: 'Set a good example and respect elders.'
choices.C: 'Use strict laws and harsh punishments so people fear you.'

questions.explanation: The Legalist would advise strict laws and harsh punishments so people fear the ruler.

questions.question: Which statement about Laozi is TRUE?
questions.explanation: Laozi is connected with Daoism.

questions.question: Which adviser is the DAOIST?

choices.A: 'Make many strict laws and punish hard.'
choices.D: 'Live simply and in harmony with nature.'

questions.explanation: The Daoist would advise living simply and in harmony with nature.

questions.question: Confucianism and Legalism both tried to do what?
questions.explanation: Both Confucianism and Legalism aimed to create order in society, though by very different means.

questions.question: Which idea would Confucius MOST likely reject?

choices.C: Ruling only by fear and cruelty

questions.explanation: Confucius favored respect and good example, so he would reject ruling only by fear and cruelty.

questions.question: China's three great philosophies were Confucianism, Daoism, and
questions.explanation: The third of China's three great philosophies was Legalism.

questions.question: Which teacher would say, 'Rulers should be feared, not just admired'?
questions.explanation: Han Fei Zi, the founder of Legalism, taught that rulers should be feared, not just admired.

questions.question: Why were Confucius's ideas so important to China?

choices.A: They guided family life and government for thousands of years

questions.explanation: Confucius's ideas guided Chinese family life and government for thousands of years.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT something Confucius taught?
questions.explanation: Ruling through harsh punishments belongs to Legalism, not Confucius's teachings.

questions.question: A government built mostly on strict written laws and tough penalties follows the ideas of
questions.explanation: A government built on strict laws and tough penalties follows Legalism.

questions.question: Which philosophy would be LEAST interested in making lots of rules?

choices.D: All of them love rules equally

questions.explanation: Daoism taught living simply rather than following lots of rules, so it would be least interested in making many rules.

questions.question: Which is the BEST summary of China's three philosophies?

choices.A: Confucianism = respect and example, Daoism = harmony with nature, Legalism = strict laws
choices.B: All three taught the same thing
choices.C: All three were about building walls
choices.D: All three were about river floods

questions.explanation: Confucianism stressed respect and example, Daoism harmony with nature, and Legalism strict laws.

10-3.title: Inventions, the Silk Roads, and the Mongols
10-3.learn:
KEY IDEAS — CHINESE INVENTIONS, THE SILK ROADS, AND THE MONGOLS

Ancient China gave the world many important INVENTIONS, including PAPER, SILK (a smooth cloth from silkworms), the magnetic COMPASS (for finding direction), and GUNPOWDER. China also built the GREAT WALL, a huge wall constructed over centuries to help defend China's northern border from invaders.

The SILK ROADS were long TRADE ROUTES that stretched across Asia, connecting China to India, the Middle East, and the Mediterranean world. They were named for the valuable Chinese silk carried along them. The Silk Roads carried Chinese goods WEST and brought new goods, ideas, and religions back EAST. They were a major example of cultural diffusion, spreading culture between distant lands.

Later, the MONGOLS, fierce horseback warriors led by GENGHIS KHAN, conquered a vast territory and built the LARGEST LAND EMPIRE in history. Although the Mongols were feared in war, they made the Silk Roads SAFER for travel and trade, which helped goods and ideas move even more freely. Remember: China = paper, silk, compass, gunpowder, Great Wall; Genghis Khan = Mongol Empire.

questions.question: Which of these was invented in ancient China?
questions.explanation: Paper was a Chinese invention.

questions.question: What were the Silk Roads?

choices.C: Long trade routes connecting China to the west

questions.explanation: The Silk Roads were long trade routes linking China to other lands.

questions.question: Who led the Mongols to build the largest land empire in history?
questions.explanation: Genghis Khan led the Mongols to their vast empire.

questions.question: Why did China build the Great Wall?

choices.C: To defend its northern border from invaders

questions.explanation: The Great Wall helped defend China from northern invaders.

questions.question: Which Chinese invention helped sailors find direction?
questions.explanation: The magnetic compass helped find direction.

questions.question: Besides goods, what did the Silk Roads spread between distant lands?
questions.explanation: The Silk Roads spread ideas and religions, not just goods.

questions.question: How did the Mongols actually HELP trade on the Silk Roads?

choices.A: They made the routes safer to travel
choices.D: They had no effect on trade

questions.explanation: Despite being feared in war, the Mongols made the Silk Roads safer.

questions.question: Why were the Silk Roads given that name?

choices.B: Valuable Chinese silk was carried along them
choices.D: They led to a city named Silk

questions.explanation: The routes were named for the silk traded along them.

questions.question: Which list contains ONLY Chinese inventions?
questions.explanation: Paper, silk, the compass, and gunpowder were all Chinese inventions.

questions.question: The Mongol Empire is described as the largest WHAT in history?
questions.explanation: The Mongols built the largest land empire in history.

questions.question: Silk is a smooth cloth made from what?
questions.explanation: Silk is a smooth cloth made from silkworms.

questions.question: What is gunpowder, one of China's inventions, used to do?
questions.explanation: Gunpowder is an explosive, used to create explosions; it was a Chinese invention.

questions.question: The spreading of culture, ideas, and goods between distant lands is called what?
questions.explanation: The spreading of culture between distant lands is called cultural diffusion.

questions.question: Which list correctly names four famous Chinese inventions?

choices.C: Ziggurats, cuneiform, the wheel, the sail
choices.D: Paper, silk, the compass, and gunpowder

questions.explanation: Paper, silk, the compass, and gunpowder were all famous Chinese inventions.

questions.question: The Silk Roads connected China to all of these EXCEPT
questions.explanation: The Silk Roads connected China to India, the Middle East, and the Mediterranean world, but not the Americas.

questions.question: The Great Wall was built mainly to protect China's which border?
questions.explanation: The Great Wall was built to help defend China's northern border from invaders.

questions.question: In which direction did the Silk Roads mainly carry Chinese goods?
questions.explanation: The Silk Roads carried Chinese goods west and brought new goods and ideas back east.

questions.question: Which sentence about the Mongols is TRUE?

choices.A: They built the largest land empire in history

questions.explanation: The Mongols built the largest land empire in history.

questions.question: Why is it surprising that the Mongols helped trade?

choices.A: Because they were known as fierce, feared warriors, yet they made trade routes safer
choices.C: Because they built the Great Wall
choices.D: Because they never left their homeland

questions.explanation: It is surprising because the Mongols were feared warriors, yet they made the Silk Roads safer for trade.

questions.question: A sailor needs to know which way is north on a cloudy day. Which Chinese invention helps?
questions.explanation: The compass helps find direction, even on a cloudy day.

questions.question: Which of these did the Silk Roads carry from west to east, back to China?
questions.explanation: The Silk Roads brought new goods, ideas, and religions back east to China.

questions.question: Genghis Khan is best remembered as the leader of which group?
questions.explanation: Genghis Khan led the Mongols.

questions.question: Which invention would be MOST useful for keeping written records?
questions.explanation: Paper would be most useful for keeping written records.

questions.question: What does the lesson say the Great Wall was built to do?

choices.B: Help defend China from northern invaders

questions.explanation: The Great Wall was built to help defend China from northern invaders.

questions.question: The Mongols were known for fighting on what?
questions.explanation: The Mongols were fierce warriors who fought on horseback.

questions.question: Which is the BEST example of cultural diffusion along the Silk Roads?

choices.A: A wall built to keep invaders out
choices.B: A new religion spreading from one land to another along the routes
choices.D: A ruler losing the Mandate of Heaven

questions.explanation: A religion spreading from land to land along the routes is an example of cultural diffusion.

questions.question: Which statement about the Silk Roads is TRUE?

choices.A: They were a single short road inside one city
choices.B: They were long trade routes stretching across Asia
choices.C: They were rivers used only for fishing

questions.explanation: The Silk Roads were long trade routes that stretched across Asia.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a Chinese invention from the lesson?
questions.explanation: Hieroglyphics were an Egyptian form of writing, not a Chinese invention.

questions.question: How could the magnetic compass change travel and trade?

choices.C: It let travelers find direction more easily, even when lost

questions.explanation: The compass let travelers find direction more easily, helping travel and trade.

questions.question: The Mongols both fought wars AND helped trade. This shows that they

choices.A: could be feared in battle yet still make trade routes safer

questions.explanation: The Mongols could be feared in battle yet still made the Silk Roads safer for trade.

questions.question: Which structure was built over centuries to defend China?
questions.explanation: The Great Wall was built over centuries to help defend China.

questions.question: What does it mean to say the Mongol Empire was the largest LAND empire in history?

choices.A: It controlled more land territory than any other empire

questions.explanation: The largest land empire means it controlled more land territory than any other empire.

questions.question: The Silk Roads were named for which valuable Chinese good carried along them?
questions.explanation: The Silk Roads were named for the valuable silk carried along them.

questions.question: Which best explains WHY the Silk Roads mattered to world history?

choices.A: They kept all cultures completely separate
choices.B: They let goods, ideas, and religions spread between distant lands
choices.C: They were used only inside China

questions.explanation: The Silk Roads mattered because they let goods, ideas, and religions spread between distant lands.

questions.question: Which pair is matched correctly?
questions.explanation: Genghis Khan is matched with the Mongol Empire.

questions.question: Why would a merchant be glad the Mongols controlled the Silk Roads?

choices.A: Because the routes were safer to travel for trade

questions.explanation: A merchant would be glad because the Mongols made the routes safer to travel for trade.

questions.question: Which Chinese invention most directly helped spread writing and record-keeping?
questions.explanation: Paper most directly helped spread writing and record-keeping.

questions.question: Which event happened LAST?

choices.B: The Silk Roads connected China to other lands
choices.C: The Mongols, led by Genghis Khan, made the Silk Roads safer
choices.D: China built the Great Wall over centuries

questions.explanation: The Mongols under Genghis Khan came later and made the already-existing Silk Roads safer for trade.

questions.question: Which is the BEST short summary of this lesson?

choices.A: China invented many things, the Silk Roads spread goods and ideas, and the Mongols built a huge empire
choices.B: China had no inventions and no trade
choices.C: The Mongols invented paper and silk
choices.D: The Silk Roads were walls around China

questions.explanation: The lesson covers China's inventions, the Silk Roads spreading goods and ideas, and the Mongols' huge empire.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT something the Silk Roads did?

choices.A: Carried goods between China and other lands
choices.C: Connected China to the Mediterranean world
choices.D: Defended China's northern border from invaders

questions.explanation: Defending the northern border was the job of the Great Wall, not the Silk Roads.
